description: We are Team Astrological, a group of developers, designers, and researchers passionate about turning complex space science into engaging, interactive web experiences. For NASA Space Apps Cairo 2026, we are tackling the "Abandoned but not Forgotten" challenge by building The Galactic History Museum—a mobile-first 3D web app where students step into the role of "Cosmic Archaeologists" to explore NASA’s resting hardware across the Moon, Mars, and deep space.
summary:
Problem:
Dozens of robotic explorers, landers, rovers, and scientific stations from past lunar and Martian missions now sit silent beyond Earth—from Viking 1 and Pathfinder to Apollo hardware and Opportunity. To students and the general public, these machines often feel distant, fragmented across technical archives, or reduced to "space junk," obscuring the engineering breakthroughs and human stories they represent.

Solution:
Galactic Museum transforms NASA's resting off-world spacecraft into an interactive, bilingual (English & Arabic RTL) digital heritage museum and educational arcade. Visitors can explore:

A Walkable 3D Odyssey Museum: Glass showcase wings for the Moon, Mars, Orbital Telescopes, and Deep Space with glowing holographic reconstructions and Connor, a voiced spatial tour guide.
Interactive 3D Hardware Inspector: 23 cataloged space vehicles and 27 historical artifacts with NASA-grounded 3D models, annotated engineering hotspots, mission timelines, and verified landing coordinates.
STEM Learning Lab & Playable Mission Arcade: Interactive physics quizzes, collectible Cosmic Passport badges, and playable missions—including AFTERLIGHT, Lunar Lander, Mars Rally, Moonfall, and Every Woman's Earth—playable on both desktop keyboards and mobile touchscreens.
details:
What does it do or how does it work?

Galactic Museum is an interactive, browser-based 3D space heritage museum and educational platform built for the "Abandoned but not Forgotten" challenge. Instead of leaving lunar and Martian exploration hardware buried in technical PDFs, visitors walk through a virtual museum and inspect real NASA spacecraft up close:

  • 3D Odyssey Museum: A multi-wing Three.js museum featuring the Central Hall, East Wing (Moon), West Wing (Mars), Observation Deck (Earth/ISS/Hubble/JWST), Research Library, and Education Zone. Clicking any glass showcase activates a live holographic reconstruction above the central podium and lets visitors zoom into the vitrine or summon Connor, our spatial audio tour guide.
  • Interactive 3D Worlds & Engineering Inspector: Visitors explore 23 space vehicles across the Moon, Mars, Outer Giants, and Observatories, and 27 detailed artifacts with interactive 3D models (GLB), annotated component hotspots (RTGs, cameras, drills, solar arrays), mission timelines, and exact landing coordinates.
  • Playable Mission Arcade & STEM Learning Lab: Visitors can test their knowledge with physics challenges, earn Cosmic Passport badges, and play 5 in-app space games (AFTERLIGHT, Lunar Lander, Mars Rally, Moonfall, and Every Woman’s Earth) plus NASA Space Place simulations—all playable on desktop or mobile touchscreens.

What benefits does it have?

  • Turns static archives into hands-on exploration: Replaces dense tables with interactive 3D inspection, spatial audio storytelling, and mission gameplay.
  • Accessible across devices and languages: Runs directly in any modern browser without downloads, supports full English and Arabic localization, and includes responsive mobile touch controls and landscape guidance so phone users can explore and play seamlessly.
  • Scientifically grounded clarity: Every artifact uses transparent mission status classifications (Operational, Inactive, Lost Contact, Partially Retrieved, Impact) backed by official NASA sources.

What is the intended impact of the project?

Designed for students (ages 10–16), educators, and space enthusiasts worldwide—especially Arabic- and English-speaking learners who rarely see interactive 3D STEM archives in both languages—Galactic Museum aims to:

  1. Reframe dormant spacecraft on the Moon and Mars from "space junk" into historic monuments of human curiosity and engineering.
  2. Spark STEM interest by connecting historical missions (Apollo, Viking 1, Surveyor 3, Opportunity, InSight, Perseverance) to playable physics simulations.
  3. Provide an extensible archive ready to add upcoming Artemis and future planetary surface sites.

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?

  • Languages & Core Web Stack: TypeScript, HTML5/CSS3, React 18, Vite 6, Tailwind CSS 3, React Router 6, Zustand 5.
  • 3D Graphics & Animation: Three.js, @google/model-viewer, PlayCanvas (playcanvas, @playcanvas/react), GSAP + ScrollTrigger.
  • Audio & Voice: Web Audio API, spatial positional audio (THREE.PositionalAudio), ElevenLabs speech synthesis (for Connor’s bilingual tour narration), and CC BY 3.0 ambient soundtrack ("Aurora" by Stellardrone).
  • Datasets & References: NASA Planetary Data System (PDS), NASA 3D Resources, NASA Image and Video Library, Apollo Lunar Surface Journal (ALSJ), and NASA JPL Mission Archives.
  • Development Hardware & Tooling: Standard Windows development PCs, Git/GitHub, Node.js, and Chromium DevTools for desktop/mobile WebGL testing.

How is your project creative?

  • Museum + Holo-Deck + Arcade in One Experience: Rather than building a standard info website or a single standalone game, we combined an architectural 3D museum (Odyssey), an interactive 3D engineering teardown inspector, a cinematic planetary chronicle, and a playable mission arcade into one cohesive story.
  • Unified Curatorial Voice: Connor, our holographic guide, connects architectural wings, historical breakthroughs, and playable kiosks through synchronized spatial audio and subtitles.
  • Reframing Debris as Heritage: Even status badges and glass vitrine placards mirror real-world museum curation—honoring machines like Viking 1, Surveyor 3, and Opportunity as enduring monuments.

What factors did your team consider?

  • Historical & Scientific Accuracy: We audited 3D models, coordinates, power sources, and mission timelines against NASA PDS and JPL records (for example, ensuring Viking 1 displays its authentic lander mesh, Chryse Planitia coordinates, dual SNAP-19 RTG specs, and 2,245-sol lifespan).
  • Performance & Mobile Usability: Large 3D scenes use pooled dynamic lighting (8 fixed Three.js PointLight slots), Draco compression, lazy-loaded routes, and custom on-screen multi-touch controls so mobile phones remain smooth and playable.
  • Bilingual & Cultural Inclusion: Full RTL layout mirroring, Arabic typography (IBM Plex Sans Arabic), and bilingual telemetry/subtitles make the museum native in both English and Arabic.
  • User Experience & Polish: Careful UI spacing, unobtrusive background music controls, and guided camera transitions prevent visual clutter while keeping navigation intuitive for younger learners.
